newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firm as banks dump long dollars.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firm as banks dump long dollars.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended earlier firmness at the close of trade on Friday after local banks sold dollars and foreign investors stepped into the stock market, traders said.
"No one bet that the peso would be so strong right now, so banks dumped expensive long positions," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.5 and 1.5 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.7690/7.7710 and 7.7660/7.7680 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier one centavo firmer at 7.7640/7.7670 per dollar.
Traders noted that the peso was at its strongest since mid-October 1996, and that 48-hour contracts closed 1.2 centavos firmer on the week.
Traders added that banks may even have gone short on dollars to invest in peso-denominated money market instruments over the weekend.
Benchmark 48-hour dollar contracts settled on Friday do not need to be settled until Wednesday, as U.S. markets will be closed on Monday for President's Day.
The Mexican bourse's leading IPC index was up 0.77 percent at 3,807.61 points when the foreign exchange markets closed, partly on foreign investors being encouraged by a fall in U.S. interest rates.
Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds fell to 6.53 percent, from 6.63 percent.
Dealers expected the market to be very dull on Monday as U.S. markets will be closed.
